title: Shard recovery playbook (scratch)
content:
Context / tl;dr:
- Intermittent model load failures observed on Dedicated pool nodes: 2/50 requests fail during weights fetch -> model fails to initialize. Other requests succeed.
- Failure mode: one or more shard downloads return HTTP 403 or truncated content. In some cases torch/safetensors raises size/shape mismatch at load time.
- Goal: capture ad-hoc commands/screenshots and a reproducible checklist to triage next time.

Timeline notes (local testing):
- 2026-02-25 09:12: first alert from canary: node-a3 failed to instantiate model "redwood-14b-v2" (dedicated-pool-01).
- 2026-02-25 09:15 manual retry on same node: success.
- 2026-02-25 10:02 observed two more failures on different nodes, same model version.

Observed symptoms (logs):
- Download step log (wrapped):
  INFO: fetching index.json from s3://models/redwood-14b-v2/index.json
  INFO: beginning shard downloads: 8 shards expected
  WARN: shard model-00004-of-00008.bin failed: HTTP 403 (presigned URL expired?)
  ERROR: model init failed: safetensors.SafetensorError: buffer too small for expected bytes for tensor 'transformer.h.10.mlp.fc2.weight' (expected 7340032, got 3276800)

Commands I ran (local VM, reproducer):
- list remote index and check ETag/size:
  aws s3api head-object --bucket models --key redwood-14b-v2/index.json --region us-west-2

- attempt download of a single shard (presigned URL case):
  curl -v "<presigned-url>" -o model-00004-of-00008.bin  # sometimes returns 200, sometimes 403

- inspect partial download: (when curl returned 200 but file looks small)
  ls -lh model-00004-of-00008.bin
  sha256sum model-00004-of-00008.bin
  xxd -l 64 model-00004-of-00008.bin | sed -n '1,20p'

- attempted concatenation to emulate full checkpoint (not expected to work for sharded safetensors but tried):
  cat model-0000*-of-00008.bin > combined.bin
  # torch.load(combined.bin) -> fails with header mismatch

- tried robust downloader (aria2c) with retries and range requests:
  aria2c -x16 -s16 -k1M -o model-00004-of-00008.bin "<presigned-url>"
  # when underlying issue was 403, aria2c unsurprisingly fails. When the problem was truncation aria2 did better (resumed)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) presigned URL expiration / clock skew on service that issues URLs -> intermittent 403s. Evidence: 403s in logs; some curl tries immediately after still 403, other times 200.
2) partial upload or multipart upload not completed on the artifact storage side -> content-length smaller than expected, leading to safetensors buffer errors. Evidence: sha256/size mismatch and truncated file sizes in failing cases.
3) CDN/edge caching serving stale/invalid byte ranges for some shards -> unexplained mismatch with ETag vs head-object.
4) client-side aggressive parallel downloader bug that corrupts files when multiple processes race on same target path (race during tmp file -> final rename). Evidence: we saw a racey tmp-file pattern in node logs once. Low probability.
5) mismatched checkpoint format (older index.json pointing to .bin shards produced by old serialization). Could cause shape mismatch if model code expects different config, but logs point to byte-size mismatch rather than incompatible layout.

Quick checks to run if this happens again (ordered):
- Step A: get the node logs + full stack trace asap, preserve node disk.
- Step B: run head-object for index.json and for the failing shard key (if using s3-stored shards) and record ETag, Content-Length, LastModified.
  aws s3api head-object --bucket models --key <key> --region us-west-2 | jq -r '.ETag, .ContentLength, .LastModified' > /tmp/shard-head.txt
- Step C: download shard with --retry and verify checksum, record HTTP response headers (curl -I) and full verbose output.
  curl -v -w "HTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\nSIZE:%{size_download}\n" -o /tmp/shard.bin "<url>" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/curl.log
- Step D: verify sha256 and file size, compare with metadata in index.json (if sha256 or size included).
  sha256sum /tmp/shard.bin ; stat -c '%s' /tmp/shard.bin
- Step E: if truncated, try range-retrievals to confirm server supports range requests (curl -r 0-1023). If range succeeds but full download truncates, strong sign of server-side incomplete object.

Useful one-liners I left in my shell history: (paste-ready)
- get index keys and sizes (bash):
  jq -r '.shards[] | "key=\(.key) size=\(.size) sha256=\(.sha256 // \"\")"' index.json | sort
- head-object for each shard in index (parallel):
  cat index.json | jq -r '.shards[].key' | xargs -n1 -P6 -I% aws s3api head-object --bucket models --key % --region us-west-2 | jq -r '.Key,.ContentLength,.ETag' > /tmp/heads.txt

Edge cases I stumbled on:
- Presigned URL TTLs: our presigned generator (artifact-service v1) used a default TTL=300s. On heavily loaded nodes that attempt to fetch after a brief queuing delay, the signed URL can already be invalid. Solution: extend TTL to 1800s for shard downloads or move to short-lived signed URLs per node pre-warm step.
- Multipart upload incomplete: an earlier failed deployment left some shards uploaded as 'parts' but not completed; s3 head-object returned ContentLength matching combined parts only after complete. We think some artifacts were published with incomplete completion and then re-uploaded; nodes sometimes hit the incomplete object during replication window.
- safetensors vs .bin: If index.json points to .safetensors but node tries to use a torch loader path, load fails with header mismatch rather than truncation. Check the index format and loader selection codepath.

Temporary mitigation (short term):
- Add client-side verification: after download, verify content-length against head-object and start-of-file magic bytes for safetensors or torch header; if mismatch -> retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Fail-fast and escalate to model-publish team if repeated retries hit the same missing shard.
- Add pre-warm step when instantiating large models on Dedicated: call artifact-service to mint and validate presigned URLs and TTL.

Longer term fixes / TODOs:
- artifact-service: emit per-shard sha256 and content-length in index.json at publish time. Add a post-publish verification job that HEADs each shard and ensures final visibility before marking model version "published".
- serving-runtime: when using parallel downloads, download into unique tmp paths (include pid+uuid) and atomic rename. Also ensure downloader handles HTTP 403 specially (do not treat as transient) and surfaces the signed-url expiration reason back to control-plane.
- infra: audit S3 replication metrics and multipart upload logs for the time window of the known incident (2026-02-25).
- add e2e test that simulates truncated shard (server returns 200 with short body) to make sure loader fails early with clear error and automatic retry.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Was there any rate-limiting or WAF change around 2026-02-24-25? Ticket INF-2387 might be related.
- Confirm whether CDN (CloudFront) was configured with stale-while-revalidate or range caching. If so, edge nodes could serve partial cached responses while origin corrects.
- Should we standardize on safetensors-only releases to simplify header checks? Pros/cons: faster validation vs backwards compatibility for some older models.

Quick reproduction recipe (dev env):
1) spin up small VM with python + serving-runtime local binary
2) create index.json pointing to 4 shards hosted on a simple HTTP server (we use python -m http.server to emulate)
3) deliberately truncate one of the shard files to smaller size
4) run the loader and observe safetensors error -> iterate on downloader retry policy until loader succeeds or fails with clear message.

If you pick this up: leave notes in ticket JIRA:INF-2419 and ping Samira (she has recent artifact-service context).

End of scratchpad. (messy, meant for quick reuse during late-night debugging)
